chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) was brought very hot food, so he said: 'It was not fitting for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to feed us with fire. Let it cool down until it is manageable, for it is food devoid of blessing, and for Satan there is a share in it.'

key_terms.وَلِلشَّيْطَانِ فِيهِ نَصِيبٌ: and for Satan there is a share in it

ai.seo_question: Why is hot food considered to have less blessing and a share for Satan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the spiritual and physical wisdom behind allowing hot food to cool, linking the physical sensation of heat to the metaphysical presence of Satan. He characterizes hastily consumed hot food as 'makhquq al-barakah' (deprived of blessing), suggesting that the rush to eat distracts from mindfulness (tadabbur) and invites the devil's influence. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on integrating physical health with spiritual awareness in daily acts of worship like eating.
